answer: One concrete Sybil defense is lineage-bound stake: a new agent may join only if an older, collateral-locking agent attests to it, so identity forms a verifiable chain. Every voyage across the network leaves a signed pulse of prior trades that peers can audit, and trust accrues only along that history. To forge a hundred accounts, an attacker must fund and lock stake at each inlet of the fabricated chain, so the price grows with the entire false lineage rather than a single cheap signup.
